Your eleven projects 60.8 points, rising to 69.0 with Haaland as captain—a slim 0.3 points clear of Salah, though Haaland carries a notably higher ceiling, with a 25% chance of reaching 10 points against Salah's implied odds.

Arsenal's three-man presence (Raya, Gabriel, Saka) and the paired stakes in Liverpool and Manchester City mean your fortunes rest heavily on how those three clubs perform this week. Your bench is thin; Mykolenko is your only realistic cover at 3.1, so the starting XI will almost certainly play out.

No transfer clears the cost of making it. The model has tested moves and found none worth a points hit. Sit tight this week.

Your eleven projects 60.8 points. Haaland carries the armband at 8.2, a narrow 0.3 clear of Salah, with a quarter chance of breaking double figures but also an 8% tail risk of returning 2 or fewer. The projection lifts to 69.0 with the armband applied.

You are heavy on Arsenal and Manchester City — three in the eleven and two respectively — but the bench offers limited safety valve. Mykolenko at 3.1 is your best cover, a material drop from the starters. Anderson and Muniz project under 3.

You have one free transfer and £0.5m in the bank. The model found no move that clears its cost, so you are holding. That means reviewing the armband choice is your only lever. Salah at 7.9 is close enough that the read on Haaland's floor — that 8% chance of 2 or fewer — is worth weighing against a steadier alternative if you have conviction he will underperform.

Your team projects 69.0 with Haaland captained. He carries genuine upside — a 25% chance of double figures — but also real downside at 8%, so the armband is a reasonable gamble rather than a certainty. Salah sits only 0.3 behind, a reminder that you lack a clear-cut premium choice this week.

You are heavy on Arsenal and Manchester City, with three and two players respectively. That concentration is a choice you've made and it's working; all six project cleanly. The bench is thin — Mykolenko at 3.1 is your only meaningful cover — so injuries to Raya, Gabriel or Gvardiol would hurt badly.

No transfer improves your score after its cost, so you hold and bank the transfer. The team is balanced across the outfield, with your midfield doing most of the work. Palmer and Semenyo at 6.0 and 4.8 are your main questions mark: neither is projecting poorly, but neither is pulling weight like Salah and Saka.

A squad built to score in the 60s is in decent shape. You're well-placed if your premiums fire and your City wall holds.
